newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MARSEILLE LOOK TO RESTORE ASCENDANCY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MARSEILLE LOOK TO RESTORE ASCENDANCY.

text.p: Fallen French giants Marseille spent two years languishing in the second division and are anxiously looking forward to renewing major rivalries in the top flight with the likes of Paris St-Germain, Monaco and Auxerre.

Champions Auxerre's visit to the Velodrome on Sunday is their first in the league since they soundly beat Marseille 3-0 on November 20, 1993 with goals by the since departed Corentin Martins and Christophe Cocard and current striker Lilian Laslandes.
By then Marseille were under investigation for trying to rig a league match during their successful European Cup campaign the previous season.
Marseille were stripped of their 1993 league title, a record fifth in a row, and relegated as punishment at the end of the 1993-94 season. But they were allowed to keep the European Cup title.

As club owner and controversial politician Bernard Tapie sunk deeper in the mire of the match-rigging scandal, his players salvaged some pride with a 2-2 draw away to Auxerre in the return fixture on April 30, 1994, the two clubs' last league encounter.

Provincial Auxerre, the opposite to port city giants Marseille in terms of resources, style and the profile of their players, continued their steady climb in both domestic and continental stature in Marseille's absence.

Now European Cup quarter-finalists, Auxerre made one trip to the Velodrome during the disgraced Marseille's two seasons in the second division, winning a French Cup semifinal there on penalties earlier this year.
Auxerre went on to clinch the league and cup double in May, emulating the Marseille side of 1989 spearheaded by Jean-Pierre Papin.
Papin, who moved on to AC Milan, Bayern Munich and now Bordeaux, is the kind of striker sorely missed at Marseille these days as they struggle to slot back into the rhythm of the first division.
A 0-0 result when they travelled to Auxerre in August has been followed more recently by a string of goalless draws in the league, three in their last six matches.

Striker Xavier Gravelaine, one of several big signings made in the off-season to strengthen the squad for the rigours of the first division, has not delivered as expected with only five goals out of 13th-placed Marseille's total of 19 in 21 matches.
The former French international's commitment was questioned by fans during an early season slump. Midfielders Reynald Pedros and Bulgaria's Yordan Lechkov were also criticised.
However, the goalless draws are part of an unbeaten run of six matches that have steadied a rocking boat.
Even Lechkov, consigned to the bench in the league and expected to go on the transfer list, put in a fine playmaking performance in Marseille's League Cup win over Auxerre on Tuesday.
"It's very good to start the Burgundy week with a win," said Marseille executive director Jean-Michel Roussier.
The coincidence of both sides meeting twice in the same week at the same ground could backfire on hosts Marseille.
Marseille's all out efforts to win on Tuesday against an Auxerre side not at full strength may have shown their hand to coach Guy Roux, who has a particular dislike for the Mediterranean club.
Roux has in the past accused Marseille, and especially the rich Tapie, of plundering Auxerre's exemplary youth scheme to build their own line-up.

During 35 years at the Auxerre helm, Roux has helped mould a string of big name players who went on to grace the Velodrome stage, among them Eric Cantona and defender Basile Boli, whose headed goal won Marseille the ultimate crown, the European Cup.
